reproduction_target: Statistical-genetics methods demonstration of a tree-based BLUP (TBLUP) that models haplotype values and mutation effects on a local DNA tree, compared against SNP-BLUP/GBLUP. Computational pipeline: (i) retrieval of cattle mtDNA sequences from the 1000 Bull Genomes Project Run8 (ENA PRJEB42783, 'the 1KB dataset') and of seven outgroup/reference mtDNA sequences from GenBank; (ii) MAFFT alignment, Gblocks 0.91b alignment refinement, and est-sfs ancestral-allele inference; (iii) mtDNA local-tree inference with the Python package tsinfer/tskit; (iv) a 36-scenario x 100-replicate simulation of mutation, branch, haplotype and phenotype values on the inferred tree in R; (v) SNP-BLUP and TBLUP model fitting with the R package INLA and accuracy/elapsed-time evaluation; (vi) empirical analysis of the Croatian Holstein mtDNA + milk-production dataset ('CRO', from Brajkovic et al. ref [83]). All wet-lab sequence and phenotype generation was performed by the two upstream source studies and is out of scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from the bioRxiv JATS XML full text (WebFetch returned HTTP 403 for both the .source.xml and the v1.full HTML; the XML was retrieved via curl with a browser User-Agent and tag-stripped). The code repository landing page https://github.com/HighlanderLab/gmafrafortuna_quangen_tree was read at PROSE level only (README + top-level listing via the GitHub REST API): top level is .gitignore, LICENSE (GPL-3.0), README.md, helper_functions.R, plus directories ancestral_alleles/, real_data/, simulation/. No requirements.txt, no environment.yml, no renv.lock, no Dockerfile, no release tags (releases API returns an empty array), no commit pin cited in the paper. Version pins that exist are scattered: 'Gblocks 0.91b' in Methods prose, 'tskit ... Version 0.6.4' and 'Matrix ... R package version 1.7-3' in the reference list; tsinfer, est-sfs, MAFFT, INLA, R and Python carry no version. No RNG seed is stated anywhere for the 100-replicate simulation. Upstream physical sequencing/phenotyping for the 1KB and CRO datasets counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Retrieval of complete cattle mtDNA sequences (1,842 animals; 4,540 sites, 3,518 biallelic SNPs) from the 1000 Bull Genomes Project Run8, 'available at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/PRJEB42783' — no extraction tool or version named in prose

Retrieval of seven reference mtDNA sequences from GenBank (NCBI) with explicit accessions: Bos taurus V00654, Bos indicus NC_005971, Bos primigenius NC_013996, Bos grunniens KR011113, Bison bison NC_014044, Ovis aries KR868678, Camelus bactrianus ferus EF212038 — no retrieval tool or version named

Multiple sequence alignment of the seven reference mtDNA sequences with Mafft 'using default settings'; a poorly aligned portion of the D-loop discarded, giving a 16,882 bp alignment — no MAFFT version pinned

Alignment refinement with Gblocks 0.91b, 'Parameters were set for the least stringent selection', final alignment 16,327 bp — exact tool version pinned in Methods prose, but the individual Gblocks flags are described only qualitatively and no environment closure is claimed

Ancestral-allele inference with est-sfs (outgroups bison, yak, camel; cattle allele counts from 1KB; major allele called ancestral at posterior probability > 0.9, minor at < 0.1, outgroup-major fallback in between; ancestral state determined for 3,257 polymorphic sites) — no est-sfs version pinned

mtDNA local-tree inference with the Python package tsinfer (recombination_rate = 1e-20, mismatch ratio = 1e18 to force resolution by recurrent mutation), analysed with tskit; resulting tree has 124 edges, 357 sites, 411 mutations — tskit 'Version 0.6.4' appears only in the reference list, tsinfer and Python themselves carry no version pin

Simulation on the inferred 1KB mtDNA tree in R: 36 scenarios (ALL/FEW x DIFF/SAME/SYM x three phenotyping scenarios of 1,669 / 417 / 70 phenotyped animals, plus Recent vs Old&Recent), 100 replicates each; mutation effects drawn from a normal distribution and accumulated along branches — no RNG seed stated, R unpinned (Matrix 1.7-3 and tidyverse/lubridate appear only in the reference list)

SNP-BLUP and TBLUP model fitting on the simulated data with the R package INLA, plus accuracy (correlation of true vs estimated haplotype/node/branch/mutation/site effects) and elapsed-time evaluation — no INLA or R version pinned and no hyperprior specification given in prose

Empirical analysis of the CRO dataset (359 SNPs, 96 unique Croatian Holstein mtDNA sequences linked to 3,040 females, 7,576 lactation records, pedigree of 6,336 animals; from ref [83]) with SNP-BLUP and TBLUP in INLA, including inla.posterior.sample with 1,000 Monte Carlo samples for derived variance components — no accession, repository, or access route is stated for the CRO genotype/phenotype/pedigree data; the Availability statement covers scripts only

headline.static_readiness: 0/9 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 1/9 computational steps (C4, the only step whose tool carries an exact version pin in Methods prose: Gblocks 0.91b). 7/9 steps cap at NI because the tool actually invoked carries no version pin (MAFFT, est-sfs, tsinfer, INLA, R, Python; tskit 0.6.4 and Matrix 1.7-3 are pinned only in the reference list, not for the invoking step). C9 is X: the CRO real genotype/phenotype/pedigree dataset has no accession, repository, or stated access route, so that analysis cannot be re-run at all. No lockfile, container, conda spec, or release tag is claimed by the paper or the README, so even under stage-2 execution no step could exceed RI without a newly created environment capture.
headline.coverage: 9 computational steps assessed from the bioRxiv v1 JATS full-text Methods prose plus the public code-repository landing page/README prose. 2 upstream physical steps counted in W and not verdicted: whole-genome sequencing of the 1,842 1000 Bull Genomes Run8 animals, and mtDNA genotyping + milk-production phenotype/pedigree recording of the Croatian Holstein (CRO) cattle in the source study [83].
